caption_draft: Model P(official open = UP) trajectories and direction accuracy by prediction time. Top: one line per day over 37 trading days (2026-05-19 to 2026-07-13), x-axis time of day (ET, 00:00 to 9:29), y-axis model P(up); green lines are days that officially opened up, red opened down, with dots at the right edge marking the official outcome. The two 9:29 misses are highlighted: 2026-07-10 (official +4.00 pts) and 2026-06-22 (official -0.14 pts). Bottom: direction accuracy (%) versus prediction time -- the hourly sample (n=134 days) rises from about 74% at midnight to 92% at 9:00, and the minute-level sample (n=18 days) reaches about 94% near 9:29, against a 96.3% ceiling attainable with perfect 9:30 market data (residual auction noise) and the 50% coin-flip floor.

caption_draft: Stake economics for the first_signal rule (0.70 confidence gate): flat stakes swept from $25 to $2,000 with the calibrated execution model, bankroll unbound. Left: total PnL versus intended stake per trade -- test half (58 days, blue) reaches about $5.0k and all 115 days (green) about $13.2k at $2,000; the shaded region above roughly $400 marks where the impact model leaves its validated $100-500 calibration range. Middle: ROI per dollar staked -- flat at about 15.5% from $25 to $300, peaking near 19.6% (test) around $750, then declining. Right: effective stake actually placed versus intended -- fills bend away from the 1:1 line and asymptote to roughly $1,000, the liquidity ceiling of about 1% of a day's traded volume.

caption_draft: Bankroll trajectories for the $50-stake daily strategy on the test half (Apr 16 - Jul 14, 2026): hour-4 hold rule (enter at 04:00 ET when model edge >= 5c and traded-side confidence >= 0.60, hold to resolution), 21 trades, 19 wins - 2 losses, execution modeled with 1c half-spread and 0.1% impact per $100. Raw $50/day (blue) grows $100 to $264; the guarded variant staking min($50, 20% of bankroll) (green) grows $100 to $176. Dots mark the two losing days -- Jul 2 (news reversal) and Jul 10 (quirk day). caption_draft: Reliability diagram for the production model at the 9:00 ET prediction time, held-out test half of the validated 200-day window (n=100 days, 2026-02-12 to 2026-07-13; model fitted on the first 100 days, 2025-09-09 to 2026-02-11). Top: predicted P(up) binned into deciles versus the observed frequency of UP opens, with 95% Wilson intervals per bin; the dashed diagonal is perfect calibration. Bottom: days per bin -- the distribution is bimodal (24 days below 0.1 and 24 above 0.9), so most 9:00 calls are near-certain and correct (0/34 UP in the two lowest bins, 34/34 in the two highest). Brier score 0.0696. The 9:29 prediction time cannot be evaluated: minute-level history exists only as an unretained 18-day sample.

caption_draft: Day-resampled bootstrap bands for the two headline bankroll records on the test half (58 days, 2026-04-16 to 2026-07-14), 10,000 resamples of whole days with replacement, execution modeled with 1c half-spread and 0.1% impact per $100. Solid lines are the actual trajectories, dotted lines the bootstrap median, shading the 5th-95th percentile envelope. First-signal at flat $50 stakes (blue) ends at $321.53 actual; bootstrap end values 5th $95.60 / median $326.60 / 95th $491.64. Hour-4 hold staking 10% of bankroll (green) ends at $135.92 actual; bootstrap end values 5th $94.87 / median $136.67 / 95th $191.28. Both 5th percentiles sit just below the $100 start: roughly one resample in twenty ends at a small loss, the priced-in cost of 2 losing trades in 21-28 resampled at unlucky frequencies.
